stem: Which of the following physical quantities has the same dimensional formula as that of impulse?
solution: Impulse \(= F\,\Delta t = [MLT^{-2}][T] = [MLT^{-1}]\). Linear momentum \(= mv = [M][LT^{-1}] = [MLT^{-1}]\). The two match. Pressure is \([ML^{-1}T^{-2}]\), force is \([MLT^{-2}]\) and work is \([ML^{2}T^{-2}]\). Matches option B.

stem: The dimensional formula for Universal Gravitational Constant (G) is:
solution: From \(F = \dfrac{G m_1 m_2}{r^{2}}\) we get \(G = \dfrac{F r^{2}}{m_1 m_2} = \dfrac{[MLT^{-2}][L^{2}]}{[M^{2}]} = [M^{-1} L^{3} T^{-2}]\). Matches option A.
reviewNote: DUP of bank row 5deaac34 (NDA 1 2022 PYQ, 'What is the dimension of gravitational constant?') — same question, same answer, only the distractors differ. Kept for OMR parity; stays PRIVATE.

stem: Light year is a unit used for measuring:
solution: A light year is the distance travelled by light in vacuum in one year, roughly \(9.46 \times 10^{15}\) m. Despite the word 'year' in its name it is a unit of length, used for astronomical distances. Matches option C.
reviewNote: DUP of bank rows 6cef58cb and 005c8378 (NDA 2 2017 / NDA 1 2018 PYQ) — same question, same answer. Kept for OMR parity; stays PRIVATE.

stem: Which pair of physical quantities does NOT have identical dimensions?
solution: Work and torque are both \([ML^{2}T^{-2}]\); impulse and momentum are both \([MLT^{-1}]\); stress and pressure are both \([ML^{-1}T^{-2}]\). But force is \([MLT^{-2}]\) while surface tension is force per unit length, \([MT^{-2}]\), so this pair does not match. Matches option D.
reviewNote: MAYBE-dup of bank row 24bd737d (same 'which pair is not identical' framing, and the keyed answer there is tension vs surface tension). Kept as new: only 2 of 4 options are shared and the keyed option text differs.

stem: The unit of Planck's constant (h) is equivalent to the unit of:
solution: From \(E = h\nu\), \(h = \dfrac{E}{\nu} = \dfrac{[ML^{2}T^{-2}]}{[T^{-1}]} = [ML^{2}T^{-1}]\). Angular momentum \(= mvr = [M][LT^{-1}][L] = [ML^{2}T^{-1}]\). Both are joule-second. Matches option B.

stem: If energy (E), velocity (V), and time (T) are chosen as fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula of Surface Tension will be:
solution: Surface tension is force per unit length, \([MT^{-2}]\). Write \([MT^{-2}] = E^{a} V^{b} T^{c}\) with \(E = [ML^{2}T^{-2}]\) and \(V = [LT^{-1}]\). Comparing M: \(a = 1\). Comparing L: \(2a + b = 0\), so \(b = -2\). Comparing T: \(-2a - b + c = -2\), giving \(-2 + 2 + c = -2\), so \(c = -2\). Hence \([E V^{-2} T^{-2}]\). Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following is a dimensionless quantity?
solution: Strain is the ratio of change in dimension to original dimension, so it is a pure number and dimensionless. Specific resistance (resistivity) is \([ML^{3}T^{-3}A^{-2}]\), gravitational potential is \([L^{2}T^{-2}]\) and coefficient of viscosity is \([ML^{-1}T^{-1}]\). Matches option B.
reviewNote: DUP of bank row acceba7a (NDA 1 2025 PYQ, 'Which one of the following is dimensionless quantity?') — identical stem and identical keyed answer (Strain); only the distractors are harder here. Kept for OMR parity; stays PRIVATE.

stem: In van der Waals equation \(\left(P + \dfrac{a}{V^{2}}\right)(V - b) = RT\), the dimensional formula of constant a is:
solution: Only like quantities can be added, so \(\dfrac{a}{V^{2}}\) must have the dimensions of pressure. Hence \(a = P V^{2} = [ML^{-1}T^{-2}][L^{3}]^{2} = [ML^{-1}T^{-2}][L^{6}] = [ML^{5}T^{-2}]\). Matches option A.

stem: The dimensional representation of Coefficient of Viscosity \((\eta)\) is:
solution: From Newton's law of viscous flow \(F = \eta A \dfrac{dv}{dx}\), we get \(\eta = \dfrac{F}{A\,(dv/dx)} = \dfrac{[MLT^{-2}]}{[L^{2}][T^{-1}]} = [ML^{-1}T^{-1}]\). Matches option A.

stem: 1 Joule is equal to how many Ergs?
solution: \(1\ \text{J} = 1\ \text{kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}\) and \(1\ \text{erg} = 1\ \text{g cm}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}\). Converting, \(1\ \text{J} = (10^{3}\ \text{g})(10^{2}\ \text{cm})^{2}\text{s}^{-2} = 10^{3} \times 10^{4} = 10^{7}\ \text{erg}\). Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental SI unit?
solution: The seven SI base units are metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela. Tesla is a derived unit of magnetic flux density, equal to \(\text{Wb m}^{-2}\) or \(\text{kg s}^{-2}\text{A}^{-1}\). Matches option D.

stem: The dimensions of Solar Constant are:
solution: The solar constant is the radiant power incident per unit area, that is intensity. Intensity \(= \dfrac{\text{power}}{\text{area}} = \dfrac{[ML^{2}T^{-3}]}{[L^{2}]} = [MT^{-3}] = [ML^{0}T^{-3}]\). Matches option A.

stem: If velocity \(v = A + Bt + Ct^{2}\), where t is time, then the dimensions of B are:
solution: By the principle of homogeneity every term on the right must have the dimensions of velocity, \([LT^{-1}]\). So \([B][T] = [LT^{-1}]\), giving \([B] = [LT^{-2}]\), which is the dimension of acceleration. Matches option B.

stem: Dimensions of Modulus of Elasticity are identical to:
solution: Modulus of elasticity \(= \dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}}\). Strain is dimensionless, so the modulus has the dimensions of stress, which is force per unit area, that is \([ML^{-1}T^{-2}]\) — the same as pressure. Matches option C.

stem: Curie is the unit of:
solution: The curie (Ci) is a unit of radioactivity, defined as \(3.7 \times 10^{10}\) disintegrations per second. The SI unit of the same quantity is the becquerel. Matches option B.

stem: The dimension of \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}\) is equivalent to:
solution: The speed of an electromagnetic wave in free space is \(c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}\), so the expression has the dimensions of velocity, \([LT^{-1}]\). Matches option A.

stem: The ratio of SI unit to CGS unit of Force is:
solution: The SI unit of force is the newton and the CGS unit is the dyne. \(1\ \text{N} = 1\ \text{kg m s}^{-2} = (10^{3}\ \text{g})(10^{2}\ \text{cm})\text{s}^{-2} = 10^{5}\ \text{dyne}\). Matches option C.
reviewNote: MAYBE-dup of bank row eef81c32 (1 dyne equals ...) — same conversion factor, stated in the inverse direction over a disjoint option set. Kept as new.

stem: Which of the following physical quantities has the unit 'Watt-second'?
solution: Watt is the unit of power, so watt multiplied by second gives \(\text{J s}^{-1} \times \text{s} = \text{J}\), the unit of energy. Matches option B.

stem: The dimensional formula for Specific Heat Capacity is:
solution: From \(Q = m c \Delta T\), \(c = \dfrac{Q}{m \Delta T} = \dfrac{[ML^{2}T^{-2}]}{[M][K]} = [M^{0}L^{2}T^{-2}K^{-1}]\). The mass cancels, so specific heat capacity carries no dimension of mass. Matches option A.

stem: The unit 'Parsec' is used to measure:
solution: A parsec is the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arc second, roughly \(3.26\) light years or \(3.086 \times 10^{16}\) m. It is a unit of astronomical distance. Matches option B.

stem: In the relation \(F = a\sqrt{x} + b t^{2}\), where F is force, x is distance, and t is time, the dimensions of \(a/b\) are:
solution: Both terms must have the dimensions of force. From \(a\sqrt{x} = [MLT^{-2}]\), \([a] = \dfrac{[MLT^{-2}]}{[L^{1/2}]} = [ML^{1/2}T^{-2}]\). From \(b t^{2} = [MLT^{-2}]\), \([b] = \dfrac{[MLT^{-2}]}{[T^{2}]} = [MLT^{-4}]\). Dividing, \(\dfrac{[a]}{[b]} = [L^{1/2 - 1} T^{-2 + 4}] = [L^{-1/2}T^{2}]\). Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a unit of Time?
solution: Microsecond, leap year and lunar month all measure intervals of time. A light year, despite its name, is the distance light travels in one year, so it is a unit of length. Matches option D.

stem: The dimensional formula of Electric Resistance (R) is:
solution: Potential difference \(V = \dfrac{W}{q} = \dfrac{[ML^{2}T^{-2}]}{[AT]} = [ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-1}]\). By Ohm's law \(R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{[ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-1}]}{[A]} = [ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2}]\). Matches option A.

stem: The solid angle subtended by a sphere at its center has the unit:
solution: Solid angle is measured in steradian (sr), the SI supplementary unit defined as the solid angle subtending an area equal to the square of the radius. A complete sphere subtends \(4\pi\) steradian at its centre. Radian, degree and gradian are units of plane angle. Matches option B.

stem: If force F, length L, and time T are taken as fundamental units, the dimensional formula for Mass will be:
solution: Write \([M] = F^{a} L^{b} T^{c}\) with \(F = [MLT^{-2}]\). Then \(F^{a}L^{b}T^{c} = [M^{a} L^{a+b} T^{-2a+c}]\). Comparing with \([M^{1}L^{0}T^{0}]\): \(a = 1\), \(a + b = 0\) so \(b = -1\), and \(-2a + c = 0\) so \(c = 2\). Hence \([M] = [F L^{-1} T^{2}]\). This also follows directly from \(m = F/\text{acceleration}\). Matches option A.
